culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress modestly in villages, churches and cultural areas; bikinis only at private resorts or isolated beaches, and cover up with a T-shirt and sarong (lavalava) in a village. Nude or topless swimming is not acceptable. A sarong is required for men and women at formal maneaba functions. Ask before taking photos. Don't touch anyone's head, walk between people talking, or speed past a maneaba or church during a gathering.
culture-and-protocol.greetings_and_words: Say 'matauninga' (excuse me) and stoop when passing seated people. In a maneaba, sit cross-legged ('kabari'), don't turn your back on the host or point your feet at people. Guests invited to a maneaba function customarily give a gratuity (mweaka) to the master of ceremonies; on many islands a first-time visitor taken to a cultural shrine offers a stick of tobacco.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: The unimwane (elders) of the maneaba; ask through your host.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the Kiribati National Tourism Office.
